# OpenShieldHIT

> A modern, lean Monte Carlo particle transport framework written from scratch in C11. Designed to be readable, fast, and pedagogically transparent. Conceptually inspired by the same application domain as SHIELD-HIT12A; shares no code with it. MIT licensed.


OpenShieldHIT transports ions (protons, heavier ions) through 3D geometry using Continuous-Slowing-Down Approximation (CSDA), scores dose, fluence, LET, and related quantities onto Cartesian meshes or DICOM grids, and writes output in its own BDO binary format, plain text, or DICOM RTDOSE.

## Key documents

- [README.md](README.md) — overview, build, install, application usage, public C API, repository layout
- [DEVELOPER.md](DEVELOPER.md) — authoritative numbered coding ruleset (§1–§15): coding style, naming conventions, struct layout rules, C11 portability constraints (no POSIX-only APIs), module dependency rules, CMake presets
- [TODO.md](TODO.md) — known open work items; treat as directional, not authoritative (items may be stale)
- [docs/user/beam.dat.md](docs/user/beam.dat.md) — complete keyword reference for the beam input file
- [docs/user/detect.dat.md](docs/user/detect.dat.md) — scored quantities (Dose in MeV/g, DoseGy in Gy, Fluence, DLET, TLET, …) and output formats
- [docs/user/getting-started.md](docs/user/getting-started.md) — build, install, run a case

## Build

```bash
cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release --parallel   # optimised
cmake --preset debug   && cmake --build --preset debug --parallel     # plain -Og debug
cmake --preset asan    && cmake --build --preset asan    --parallel   # ASan + UBSan
ctest --test-dir build_debug --output-on-failure                      # run tests
```

There are no CTest presets — point `ctest` at the binary dir (`--test-dir build_debug`), not `--preset`.
Binaries: `build/bin/openshieldhit` (release) or `build_debug/bin/openshieldhit` (debug). Full preset table and commands: DEVELOPER.md §14.

## Running a simulation

```bash
openshieldhit path/to/case/          # full transport
openshieldhit --dry-run path/to/case/  # parse inputs only, no transport
openshieldhit -n 50000 path/to/case/   # override history count
```

A case directory must contain four plain-text input files:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `beam.dat` | Particle type, energy, beam geometry, physics switches (MCS, straggling), optional spotlist |
| `geo.dat` | GEMCA analytic geometry bodies and zones, or DICOM CT (`DCM` card) |
| `mat.dat` | Material definitions; optional external stopping-power tables via `LOADDEDX` |
| `detect.dat` | Scoring detectors: geometry, quantities, output filenames and formats |

## Source layout

```
include/openshieldhit/   public C API headers (cold workspaces, simulation entry points)
src/apps/osh/            CLI application, input-file parsers, app-level orchestration
src/beam/                beam cold workspace, runtime, wavefront spotlist
src/gemca/               analytic geometry compiler and runtime (zone/material lookups)
src/material/            material runtime, stopping-power tables
src/scoring/             scoring runtime, step accumulation, postprocessing, BDO/text/DICOM save
src/transport/           CSDA wavefront transport loop, per-step physics
src/simulation/          top-level compile + run entry points (osh_simulation_create/run/free)
src/common/              shared low-level utilities (diagnostics, file I/O, math, raytrace)
src/voxel/               CT voxel body, HU calibration, Jacobs traversal
src/physics/             MCS (Molière), energy straggling (Gaussian), nuclear interactions
tests/unit/              CTest unit tests (one binary per module)
tests/cases/             end-to-end integration cases (each is a self-contained case directory)
tests/fixtures/          small shared input files reused across unit tests
```

## Coding conventions

Coding rules are **not** duplicated here — [`DEVELOPER.md`](DEVELOPER.md) is the
authoritative, numbered ruleset (§1–§15). Cite a section (e.g. "violates §1")
rather than paraphrasing. This map points at the sections agents need most:

- C dialect, K&R top-of-block declarations, initialization — §1
- Type / `const` / boolean spelling (`struct foo`, `double const *p`) — §2
- Comments and Doxygen (block `/* */` only in production) — §4
- Return conventions (predicate `int` vs `enum osh_status`, `OSH_OK = 0`) — §5
- Naming and file layout (`osh_` prefix; `static` helpers) — §6
- Module layout and dependency direction — §9
- No allocations on the simulation hot path — §10
- Portability, banned APIs, case-insensitive keyword matching — §11

## Unit conventions

Quantities are generally in CGS-adjacent physics units (MeV, cm, g) — consistent with SH12A defaults. Exceptions exist where SI or clinical units are more natural: `DoseGy` outputs absorbed dose in Gy rather than MeV/g, and `DLET`/`TLET` are in MeV/cm. When in doubt, check the unit string in the output file header or the `page_data_unit()` function in `src/scoring/save/osh_scoring_save_bdo2019.c`.

## SH12A / DICOM compatibility notes

- BDO binary output uses the SH12A magic number `xSH12A` for legacy tool compatibility
- `USECBEAM` spotlist x/y coordinates are isocenter coordinates (SH12A / DICOM RT Plan convention); openshieldhit back-projects them to beam-start coordinates using `BEAMSAD`
- DICOM support (CT read, RTDOSE read/write) is built in — no external DICOM library required
- zlib is optional (enables compressed `.bdz` output); not related to DICOM

## IMPORTANT: relationship to SHIELD-HIT and SHIELD-HIT12A

OpenShieldHIT shares **zero source code** with SHIELD-HIT (the original code) or with SHIELD-HIT12A (SH12A).
Do NOT describe it as a "reimplementation", "port", or "derivative" of either — those terms imply code derivation and are legally incorrect.
The code flow is **one-way**: parts of OpenShieldHIT *may be reused in* SH12A, not the other way around.
The connection is limited to: same application domain, same input-file format (beam.dat / geo.dat / mat.dat / detect.dat), and conceptual inspiration.
The architecture, algorithms, and every line of OpenShieldHIT are written from scratch, using only publicly available scientific literature and data.
